title: Computational CXL-Memory Solution for Accelerating Memory-Intensive Applications
problem: CXL interface provides limited physical bandwidth that becomes a significant bottleneck for data-intensive applications. This bandwidth constraint prevents effective utilization of CXL-based memory expansion in memory-disaggregated systems.
motivation: CXL enables cost-effective memory expansion and device heterogeneity, but bandwidth limitations restrict its applicability to emerging memory-intensive workloads that require high-throughput data movement.
method: The system spreads memory across different physical locations (disaggregation) connected by CXL cables, which are high-speed links between servers and memory pools. Instead of sending all data back to the main processor, computing happens right next to the spread-out memory, which cuts the data flowing through the bandwidth-limited CXL connection. A working prototype demonstrates this approach is practical.
key_novelty: Running computation next to the disaggregated memory instead of sending all data across the bandwidth-limited CXL cable to the main processor.
contributions: CXL-based memory disaggregation architecture with integrated near-data processing
Bandwidth-efficient approach to accelerate memory-intensive applications using computational memory
Real-world prototype implementation and experimental validation
1.9x improvement in performance and power efficiency over baseline CPU systems
primary_theme: CXL memory disaggregation with near-data processing
